text: I approach the tavern runner, buy a bowl of stew, and ask, “Who went missing with that patrol?”
motivation: Follow a mundane detail into a natural social inquiry.
intended: Buy stew and ask the tavern runner who was in the missing patrol.

text: I carry the stew to the gate serjeant, offer the bowl with a smile, and ask, "Who was on the missing patrol, and what favor would loosen the roster?"
motivation: Follow the runner advice while using a small friendly gesture to learn who vanished.
intended: Ask the gate serjeant for patrol names and what favor could earn the information.

text: I drift over to the threadbare watcher and murmur, "You watch packs more than gates—did you notice anyone following the patrol before it vanished?"
motivation: The watcher seems observant in an unusual way, and may know more than official channels reveal.
intended: Learn whether the watcher saw suspicious activity connected to the missing patrol.

text: I follow the watcher gaze to the clustered packs and ask softly, "Then forget the patrol—which movement in this crowd worries you right now?"
motivation: Shift from the guarded patrol mystery to the immediate mundane pattern that has captured the watcher attention.
intended: Discover what suspicious movement or person the watcher is currently observing.

text: I leave the silent watcher be and examine the notice board closely, lifting the corners of the fresh tax and curfew sheets to see what older notices they cover.
motivation: Follow a mundane physical clue after the watcher declines to engage.
intended: Look beneath the fresh postings for older patrol notices, altered routes, names, or other overlooked information.

text: I inspect the waiting wagon wheels for the distinctive mud of that northwest track, then ask the likeliest driver, "Come through there today—anything odd along the way?"
motivation: Use an incidental physical detail to find a traveler with firsthand knowledge of the abandoned route.
intended: Identify someone who recently used the northwest track and learn what they encountered.

text: I crouch beside his wagon and ask permission to sift a little mud from the axle for leaves, fibers, or metal scraps caught near the old milestone.
motivation: The driver noticed nothing, but his wagon may have carried back small physical traces from the churned ground.
intended: Search debris on the wagon for clues about activity near the old milestone.

text: I stand, point to the axle, and ask the driver who just answered me, "Is this one yours? I will clean the axle while I look, if that makes the poking worthwhile."
motivation: Clarify ownership and offer useful labor instead of touching a guarded wagon without consent.
intended: Gain the driver permission to inspect the axle mud while cleaning it.

text: I abandon the mysterious ownerless wheel, cross to the townhouse, and knock beneath its noble colors, asking, "Does this house sponsor the gate patrols—or know why their old route changed?"
motivation: Change direction toward the conspicuously detached noble household overlooking the gate.
intended: Learn whether the townhouse has authority, funding, or information connected to the patrol routes.

text: I step back from the silent door and study the rain-softened footprints and carriage tracks leaving the townhouse, following whichever fresh trail leads toward the gate.
motivation: Let mundane physical traces answer where the deliberately silent household will not.
intended: Determine whether anyone from the townhouse recently traveled through the gate and which route they took.
